n: Alma turns his listeners’ minds back to when God first gave commandments, reminding them that God ordained priests “after the order of his Son” to teach the plan.

f.w: after the order of his Son
f.g: The higher priesthood, later called the Melchizedek Priesthood.

n: These priests’ ordinations themselves pointed people toward the Son of God for redemption.
Alma explains that priests were called and prepared before this life, according to God’s foreknowledge, because of their faith and good works. They had chosen good when left free to choose.

f.w: called and prepared from the foundation of the world

f.g: God’s knowledge of things before they happen.

n: They received this calling because of their faith. Others could have had the same privilege but rejected the Spirit through hard hearts and blind minds.

f.w: as great privilege as their brethren
f.g: Foreordination is not favoritism; the opportunity was open to all.

n: In short, all began on equal footing. The holy calling was prepared for those who would not harden their hearts, through the Atonement of Christ.
Thus called, they were ordained to the high priesthood to teach God’s commandments so others could enter his rest.

f.w: the high priesthood of the holy order of God

n: This priesthood, patterned after the Son, has no beginning or end — prepared from eternity to eternity.

f.w: without beginning of days or end of years
f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation of Hebrews 7:3 clarifies that it is the priesthood, not Melchizedek himself, that is without beginning or end.

n: They were called with a holy calling, ordained with a holy ordinance, and received the eternal high priesthood.

f.g: A sacred rite performed by authority — here, ordination.

n: Thus they become high priests forever, after the order of the eternal Son, full of grace, fairness, and truth.
Many were ordained high priests because of their great faith, repentance, and righteousness — choosing to repent rather than perish.

f.g: Even these great priests needed repentance.

n: They were sanctified, their garments washed white through the blood of the Lamb.

f.w: washed white through the blood of the Lamb

n: Purified by the Holy Ghost, they came to see sin only with revulsion. Very many were made pure and entered the Lord’s rest.

f.w: could not look upon sin save it were with abhorrence

n: Alma invites the people to humble themselves and repent so they too may enter that rest.
Be humble like the people in Melchizedek’s day. Melchizedek was a high priest of this same order.

f.g: The Joseph Smith Translation adds a longer account of Melchizedek after Genesis 14:24.

n: Abraham himself paid tithes — a tenth of everything — to Melchizedek.
These ordinances were a “type” — a symbol — of the Son of God, helping people look forward to him for forgiveness.

f.g: A type is a symbol or foreshadowing of something greater.

n: Melchizedek ruled Salem, whose people were deeply wicked.

f.g: Many identify Salem with Jerusalem; “salem” is related to the Hebrew shalom, “peace.”

n: Through mighty faith Melchizedek received the priesthood and preached repentance. His people repented, and he brought peace, so he was called the prince of peace — a title that also points to Christ.

f.w: he did reign under his father
f.g: A detail not found in Genesis.

n: Many came before and after him, but none were greater, which is why he is singled out.
Alma says enough has been said. The scriptures are before them; twisting them leads to destruction.
Alma stretches out his hand and cries: now is the time to repent, for the day of salvation is near.

f.w: Now is the time to repent

n: The Lord declares glad tidings through angels to all nations, including his scattered people — which is how the message reached the Nephites.
Because the Nephites are wanderers in a strange land, God has made the message especially plain so they cannot misunderstand.
Angels are declaring this to many in the land right now, preparing hearts to receive Christ when he comes.
Alma longs to hear angels announce Christ’s coming in his own lifetime — but sooner or later, he will rejoice in it.

f.w: Would to God that it might be in my day
f.g: A personal longing; Christ’s coming would be about 80 years later.

n: At Christ’s coming, angels will announce it to righteous people, fulfilling the prophets’ words.

f.w: made known unto just and holy men

n: Alma pleads from the depths of his heart, anxious to the point of pain, that they will not procrastinate their repentance.

f.w: procrastinate the day of your repentance

n: Humble yourselves, pray always, and you won’t be tempted beyond what you can bear. Be led by the Spirit: humble, meek, submissive, patient, and loving.

f.w: not be tempted above that which ye can bear

n: Have faith, hope for eternal life, and keep God’s love always in your hearts, so you may be lifted up at the last day.

f.w: the love of God always in your hearts

n: Alma prays that the Lord will grant them repentance so they may escape his wrath, the chains of hell, and the second death.
Mormon notes Alma said much more that isn’t recorded.

f.w: which are not written in this book
